events.text: A Concord picket, gutted and tidy. Her fire-control locker is still sealed, and stencilled on its door: SEE ALSO, FORM 9, POINT DEFENCE (REVISED).

choices.text: Copy the revised point defence drawings.

outcomes.text: The drawings are annotated in three hands, two of them furious. Point Defence Mk II, with the corrections already made.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A survey barge with a broadside of lenses where the cargo bay should be. The log says "calibration"; the burn marks say otherwise.

choices.text: Take the lens rack plans.

outcomes.text: Three lenses to a battery, firing in sequence. The Concord call it a salute. The target would call it a Tuesday.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A dreadnought keel, sliced clean from the hull, its spinal lens still mounted and still faintly warm. Someone left in a hurry and took the crew.

choices.text: Cut the lance mount free and copy its plans.

outcomes.text: The lance runs the length of the keel. The plans run to forty pages, the last of which says "face the target".

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A hull plate with five little barrels bolted along it in a row, like teeth in a jaw. Someone has chalked "MINE" on it. Someone else has chalked over that.

choices.text: Prise the strip off and take its drawings.

outcomes.text: Five barrels, one feed, and a tag in clan script: "Do not fire near your own engines." The drawings are in the margin.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A scrap barge with three flak mouths along her flank and nothing left to shoot at. Her gunner is still at the sights, in a manner of speaking.

choices.text: Take the battery plans from the gun deck.

outcomes.text: Three flak mouths, one trigger. The pellets arrive as weather. The plans are stained with something you decide is coffee.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A clan trader with a belt of slugs wound round her counter like a scarf. "Chain slug," she says, "fastest thing on the barge if you feed it."

choices.text: Buy the plans for what she asks.

outcomes.text: She wants nothing for the plans and a great deal for the lecture. You take both.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A hulk with eight little hatches in her flank, every one open. Whatever lived in them left in a hurry and took its sense of proportion.

choices.text: Strip the hatch controllers and the plans.

outcomes.text: Six small missiles, all with the same idea. Point defence has to pick one, and the rest remember it.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A torpedo rack the size of a chapel, one tube still loaded. It is pointed at nothing in particular, which is how you know it has been waiting.

choices.text: Take the plans and unload nothing.

outcomes.text: One missile the size of a closet. You copy the plans from a distance, and then from a greater distance.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A coil of rings drifting in the dark, lit one at a time from within, as if something were counting. It reaches three, and the light waits.

choices.text: Copy the capacitor winding.

outcomes.text: Three rings and the patience to fill them. Let it sit, then watch the shields leave in a row.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A drawn line of light, motionless, a kilometre long. At its source, a barrel. At its end, a very surprised asteroid.

choices.text: Trace the line back and take the barrel plans.

outcomes.text: A long beam, drawn slowly, like a ruler. Whatever it crosses gets marked.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A hull-long crystal, humming a single note. When you hum it back, a door opens in it, and in the door, a set of plans.

choices.text: Take the plans and hum quietly.

outcomes.text: Fires down the whole keel for two long seconds. The plans warn: turn the ship, then turn it off again.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.

events.text: A Concord requisitions clerk with a crate marked OBSOLETE, a smile marked INTERIM, and a rail gun marked, in pencil, "ask me".

choices.text: Ask, and take the rail plans.

outcomes.text: "Long," she says, "and fast, and nobody has ever seen it coming." She stamps the plans twice, in case.

choices.text: Leave it for someone with more patience.

outcomes.text: You leave it. The Drift will find it another owner; it usually does.
